title: Software update and software updates management system
scope_summary: This Regulation approves vehicle types with regard to their software update processes, and requires the vehicle manufacturer to hold a Certificate of Compliance for its Software Update Management System (SUMS). It applies to vehicles of categories M, N, O, R, S and T that permit software updates.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to vehicles of Categories M, N, O, R, S and T that permit software updates.
applies_to_components: Software update processes of the vehicle type
Software Update Management System (SUMS) of the vehicle manufacturer
Software updates (including changes of configuration parameters)
relation_to_other_regulations: RXSWIN definition refers to the type approval relevant software contributing to the type approval relevant characteristics of the vehicle under any other UN Regulation N° X, so software updates may affect approvals granted under other Regulations.
Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3), ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.6.
Approval mark may be combined with marks of other Regulations under which the vehicle type is approved (paragraph 4.2).

defined_terms.definition: Vehicles which do not differ in the manufacturer's designation of the vehicle type and in essential aspects of the design with respect to software update processes.

A dedicated manufacturer-defined identifier representing information about the type approval relevant software of the Electronic Control System contributing to the Regulation N° X type approval relevant characteristics of the vehicle.
A package used to upgrade software to a new version including a change of the configuration parameters.
The process of installing and activating an update that has been downloaded.
A systematic approach defining organizational processes and procedures to comply with the requirements for delivery of software updates according to this Regulation.
A person operating or driving the vehicle, a vehicle owner, an authorised representative or employee of a fleet manager or of the vehicle manufacturer, or an authorized technician.
An operating mode in case of a failure of an item without an unreasonable level of risk.
The part of an Electronic Control System that consists of digital data and instruction.
Any method of making data transfers wirelessly instead of using a cable or other local connection.
A set of components and/or sub-systems that implement a function or functions.
A representation of digital data against which comparisons can be made to detect errors or changes in the data, such as checksums and hash values.

applicability_hints: Applies to any vehicle of categories M, N, O, R, S, T that permits software updates — including trailers (O) and agricultural/forestry vehicles and equipment (R, S, T), not just cars.

Approval is of the vehicle type plus the manufacturer's organisational SUMS; individual components/ECUs are not approved separately, but any ECU whose software can be updated is in scope via the vehicle manufacturer's SUMS and vehicle requirements.
A change of configuration parameters counts as a software update, so calibration/parameter changes are covered, not only new code.
ECUs whose software contributes to type-approval relevant characteristics under other UN Regulations must be tracked via an RXSWIN; updating them can affect those other approvals.
Wireless (OTA) update capability, e.g. telematics/connectivity units, triggers additional OTA-specific requirements (safe state, user information, preconditions, integrity validation).
Suppliers of software-updatable ECUs may need to provide information under intellectual property confidentiality provisions (3.4) to support the manufacturer's approval.
Update methods by workshop/diagnostic tools (cable/local connection) are also covered, not only OTA.
